findings.claim: The eight F_CORPUS tests successfully fail on an empty or truncated registry (via F_CORPUS_001) and a naive filler registry. However, they can pass vacuously if `corpus_data.jsonl` is replaced with 17,941 synthetic dummy entries (with unique IDs and whitespace inputs) plus B-001, because the contract asserts structural bounds rather than transpilation correctness. Furthermore, F_CORPUS_007 effectively compares the loader to itself by parsing the exact same `include_str!` literal.

The lockfile correctly and completely bumps the 5 workspace members (bashrs, bashrs-oracle, bashrs-runtime, bashrs-specs, bashrs-wasm) to 7.0.2. `cargo tree --locked -p bashrs --depth 0` and `cargo check --locked --workspace` both pass without issue, confirming `--locked` will not refuse publication.

There are no blockers in this diff preventing the v7.0.2 tag or crates.io publication. The data file is properly packaged (verified via `cargo package --list`), the verification command passes, and roadmap acceptance tests pass successfully.
